captions.instagram:
How do practical special effects work?

Film rain is often heavier than a monsoon cloudburst, yet it vanishes on camera unless it is lit from behind. Run a rain bar and a wind machine, shatter a sugar-glass window, fly a performer on a counterweight, drive an animatronic's servos and fire a gas flame bar, safety checklist first.

→ Special effects happen for real on set. Visual effects are added later on a computer.
→ Real fire throws real, flickering light on the actor. Digital fire has to fake it.
→ Film rain comes from a rain bar, and it only shines on camera when it is backlit.
→ A wind machine blows rain aside, and light paper snow drifts much further.
→ Breakaway glass is weak and light, so it shatters into small, blunt pieces.

youtubeLong.title: How do practical special effects work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Film rain is often heavier than a monsoon cloudburst, yet it vanishes on camera unless it is lit from behind. Run a rain bar and a wind machine, shatter a sugar-glass window, fly a performer on a counterweight, drive an animatronic's servos and fire a gas flame bar, safety checklist first.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/e/sfxclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/sfxclear

In this video:
• SFX vs VFX. Special effects are real, physical tricks done on set, in front of the camera.
• Weather on demand. Rain bars, wind machines, paper snow and hazers make weather on cue.
• Breakaways. Sugar glass, resin bottles, balsa chairs and foam rubble look solid but break easily into light, blunt pieces.
• Rigs and wires. Wire flying hangs a harnessed performer over pulleys to a counterweight: a = (M − m) g / (M + m), with wires rated many times the load.
• Creatures and make-up. Animatronics hide servos under foam or silicone skin, driven by puppeteers out of shot with a 1 to 2 ms pulse 50 times a second.
• Fire, safety first. Film fire is mostly gas burners run by a licensed operator, with rehearsals, a fire marshal, shields and an emergency stop.
